passage: A jeep with a loudspeaker stopped at the village chowk, and Chetan, sharing a bench with the old men, heard a clip of the rival candidate saying the water tank would be sold off. His stomach clenched. He thought of his mother filling pots at dawn. By evening the clip was on every phone. Leela, who ran the seed shop, frowned at it. "It cuts off mid-sentence," she said. "Who gains if we're scared?" She listened to the full speech on the radio with Chetan, and the candidate had said the opposite. They walked to the block office, where a notice showed the tank was not being sold. "The candidate I like has flattering clips too," Leela added. "I check those as well."

qa.q: What did the clip claim would happen to the water tank?
qa.a: It claimed the water tank would be sold off.

qa.q: Why did Chetan's stomach clench when he heard the clip?
qa.a: He was afraid of losing the water, and he pictured his mother filling pots at dawn.

qa.q: Which steps helped Chetan and Leela find out the truth?
qa.a: They noticed the clip cut off mid-sentence, asked who gains from fear, listened to the full speech on the radio and checked the notice at the block office.

qa.q: How does Leela see clips that flatter her own side?
qa.a: She is wary of them too, and checks them as well.

grounding: Campaign clips and fear rumours steer emotion; Chetan learns to ask who benefits and check several sources, even for flattering content.
